TPVR.title: Two pawns against a whole rook. Who wins? #shorts
TPVR.desc:
Two connected passed pawns on the sixth rank beat a rook when the kings are too far away to help. 1...Rb1 2.c7 Rc1 3.b7 Rxc7 4.b8=Q+ Kg7 5.Qxc7+. The rook can stop one pawn, never both.

Did you bet on the rook?

#chess #chessendgame #chesstips

QRAC.title: Black makes a queen first, and White still wins #shorts
QRAC.desc:
Both pawns are one step from the last rank, and it's Black's move. 1...h1=Q 2.a8=Q+ and the king has to leave the long diagonal, so 3.Qxh1 wins the new queen. The tactic is called a skewer.

Did you see the skewer?

#chess #chessendgame #chesstactics

QRAC.ig:
Black makes a queen first, and White still wins. How? Did you see the skewer?

TRCS.title: He touched the rook first, so he wasn't allowed to castle #shorts
TRCS.desc:
Castling is a king move. Under the touch-move rule (FIDE Laws of Chess, article 4.4), a player who touches the rook first can't castle with it on that move: the rook has to move. In this example position that loses on the spot: after Rf1 or Rg1 comes Qe2#. Pick up the king first.

Has it ever happened to you?

#chess #chessrules #castling

KMAT.title: A king can never give check. This king delivers checkmate #shorts
KMAT.desc:
Edward Lasker against George Thomas, London 1912. After a queen sacrifice on h7 the black king is driven from g8 all the way to g1, and 18.Kd2 opens the back rank for the rook on a1: checkmate with a king move.

BSH3.title: Save this trap: he takes a free pawn and you checkmate him on move 7 #shorts
BSH3.desc:
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nd4 4.Nxe5? Qg5 5.Nxf7 Qxg2 6.Rf1 Qxe4+ 7.Be2 Nf3#. It's the Blackburne Shilling trap. It only works if White takes on e5: after 4.Nxd4 he is simply better.

KVTP.title: The king stands right next to two loose pawns and can't win either #shorts
KVTP.desc:
Two pawns with one file between them protect each other without any help. 1...Kc6 2.a6 Kxc5 3.a7 and the pawn queens. 1...Ka6 2.c6 Kxa5 3.c7 is the same story. The king can only wait.

Did you know this one?

#chess #chessendgame #chesstips

CSCK.title: This king was just in check, and he can still castle #shorts
CSCK.desc:
A check doesn't take castling away for good. You can't castle while you are in check, through an attacked square or into check. But once the check is blocked, castling is legal as long as the king and that rook have never moved. 1.d4 e6 2.Nf3 Bb4+ 3.c3 Be7 4.e3 Nf6 5.Bd3 O-O 6.O-O.

Did you think one check ends castling?

#chess #chessrules #castling

LGL3.title: Save this one: let him take your queen, and it's mate two moves later #shorts
LGL3.desc:
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 d6 3.Bc4 Bg4 4.Nc3 g6? 5.Nxe5 Bxd1 6.Bxf7+ Ke7 7.Nd5#. It's Légal's Mate. If Black takes the knight instead (5...dxe5), White takes the bishop on g4 and is a pawn up.
